chunks: And ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar asked his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar, peace be upon them:

About a man: is it permissible for him to lean against the wall of the mosque while he is praying, or to place his hand on the wall while standing, without illness or any ailment? He said: “There is no harm.”

And about a man who is in an obligatory salat (prayer), and rises in the first two rakʿahs: is it permissible for him to take hold of the side of the mosque and then rise, seeking help through it in standing, without weakness or any ailment? He said: “There is no harm in it.”

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible
key_terms.يَسْتَنِدَ: to lean or rest against something for support

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to lean on a wall or use support while standing in salat (prayer) without illness?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that there is no harm in a person leaning on or placing a hand against the mosque wall during salat (prayer), even without illness. It also permits using the side of the mosque for support when rising during the obligatory prayer, indicating such support does not invalidate the prayer.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.1045 - Ali ibn Ja'far asked his brother Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim (as) on whether it is permissible for a man to lean against the wall of the mosque while he is praying, or to place his hand on the wall while standing, without any illness or condition?"
He (as) replied: "There is no harm in that."

He also asked: "What about a man who is praying the obligatory prayer, and in the first two rak'ahs, he stands up and leans on the side of the mosque to help him rise, without any weakness or condition?"
He (as) replied: "There is no harm in that either."
